Resolves #18780

The keyboard now rests the way the pointer does: arrowing onto a parent item previews its submenu, and arrowing off it drops that preview — including one a hover opened. Both halves come from a single signal rather than two rules, and `ArrowRight` still enters the submenu it just opened.

`src/menu/List.mjs`: +37 / −14, one docblock line in `src/component/Base.mjs`.

Evidence: L3 (the real menu driven by real focus and real arrow keys in Chromium) → L3 required (AC-1…AC-6). No residual.

## The mechanism, in one paragraph

`manager.Focus#focusMove` fires `onFocusMove` on the **closest component the old and new paths share** (`src/manager/Focus.mjs:110`). For a move between two items of one menu that component is the menu; for a move into a submenu it is an ancestor of both menus. So a menu hears exactly the moves it should act on, and the descendant case — the one a plausible implementation gets wrong — needs no guard at all.

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | component `menu/List.spec.mjs` › focus rest › *arrowing onto a parent previews its submenu, and arrowing off it drops the preview* — asserts `aria-expanded`, that focus stays on the parent, and that the item is not selected |
| AC-2 | same arm's second half: `ArrowDown` back onto `Rename` leaves one menu and `aria-expanded="false"` |
| AC-3 | same › *CONTROL: Right into a previewed submenu keeps it open* |
| AC-4 | same › *the last rest wins, whichever input started it* — a hover opens `Share`'s submenu, the keyboard then rests on `Export`, and the arm asserts one menu showing `PDF` with `Email` gone |
| AC-5 | the file's other 14 arms, green; one of them changed behaviour by design — see Deltas |
| AC-6 | same › *showSubMenuOnHover: false suppresses the focus rest as well* |

## Deltas from ticket

**One existing arm asserted the behaviour this ticket reverses.** #18760's *"Right on a leaf, Left in the root, and Down onto a parent show nothing"* is now *"Right on a leaf and Left in the root show nothing"*; what `Down` does belongs to the focus-rest describe, where it is asserted rather than denied. A reviewer should read that hunk as the behaviour change it is.

**Naming fork, decided:** `showSubMenuOnHover` keeps its name and now governs both rests, with the config docblock saying so. The alternative (rename to `showSubMenuOnRest` while the config is a day old and unreleased) is recorded in the ticket; it is a one-line change if you would rather have it.

**Focus arriving from outside the menu is not a rest.** Only moves *within* a menu are, so opening a menu whose first item is a parent does not cascade a second level unasked. The ticket's AC-1 wording says "focus resting"; this is where that line was drawn, and the arms place focus with `.focus()` before arrowing precisely so they measure a move.

`component.Base`'s `onFocusMove` docblock advertised `opts.newPath`. `manager.Focus` passes `{component, path, oldPath}`, and a repo-wide census found no implementer to disagree with — this diff is the first. Corrected rather than worked around.

|---|---|
| hide on focus leave | the CONTROL arm **alone** — the other three pass, which is the whole reason that arm exists |

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**What I verified rather than accepted — the `component.Base` change is a documentation *repair*, and it was wrong before this PR.**

The diff rewrites the `onFocusMove` hook's JSDoc: `opts.newPath` → `opts.path`, plus `opts.component` and "fires on the closest component the old and new focus paths share". A doc edit in the class every component extends is exactly where I would expect a signature bent to fit a new consumer, so I read the producer. `manager/Focus.mjs:107-117`:

```js
component = Neo.getComponent(commonId);
data = {component, path: opts.data.path, oldPath: history[0].data.path};
component.onFocusMove?.(data);
```

So the payload really is `{component, path, oldPath}`, dispatched on the closest common component. **The old docblock was simply wrong** — an implementer trusting it would have destructured `newPath` and got `undefined`.

Enumerated who could have been bitten, rather than assuming nobody: `git grep onFocusMove` outside `manager/Focus.mjs` returns exactly two hits — the stub being fixed here, and `test/playwright/unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs:40`, which already reads `data.component.id`, `data.oldPath`, `data.path`. **The spec knew the real shape and the documentation contradicted it**; `menu.List` is the first production implementer, so no consumer carried the bug. A hook documented wrong and only falsified when something finally used it — worth a `[KB_GAP]` below.

**And the claim I came in most sceptical about is pinned by your control, not by my reasoning.** The docblock asserts that `ArrowRight` moving focus *into* a submenu shares an ancestor of both menus and so never reaches `onFocusMove` — which is the only reason the newly-opened level survives. I was going to verify that structurally from the floating-component parenting. I did not need to:

> `CONTROL: Right into a previewed submenu keeps it open` — *"a rule that hides whenever focus leaves the parent would close the level it just opened, and this is the only arm that can tell the two rules apart"*

That is the discriminating arm, and naming *why* it is the only one is what stops a later reader deleting it as redundant with the others.

**Challenge (non-blocking):** `onFocusMove` fires on the closest common component, so a menu's rest now starts from any focus move that resolves to it — today only item-to-item, because items are the only focusable children. If a menu ever gains a focusable non-item child (a search field at the top, a footer action), `getInteractiveItemIndex` returns `undefined` and `startRest` is correctly skipped — so the behaviour is right, but the *pending* rest from the previous item is then also not cancelled, since `cancelRest()` lives inside `startRest`. Not reachable today and not worth a guard on speculation; worth knowing if a non-item child ever lands.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):**

- [x] `startRest`'s summary states the mechanism (*"One timer for both, so the last rest wins whichever input started it"*) rather than the outcome.
- [x] `onFocusMove`'s docblock explains the dispatch rule it depends on, which is the non-obvious part, and is accurate against `manager/Focus.mjs`.
- [x] The `component.Base` doc now matches its producer — verified at source, in both directions.

**Findings:** Pass.
